The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Monday at 29,023.18, down 0.98%, inside a 28,875.97-29,151.97 range and about 147 points above the session low, while the Dow rose 0.26%. VIX is 15.85 after a 4.76% rise inside a narrow 15.61-16.06 band, WTI is about 85.02 after falling 2.35%, and the 10-year yield eased roughly 3.5 basis points to 4.70%. Tail is 8 in the low band because there is no gap, no session-extreme holding, no repeated extension after failed retracements and no aligned cross-asset confirmation. Stress is 43 in the moderate band because Tuesday's US calendar carries no Tier-1 release. Confidence is 85.
recommendation: Descriptive: the reopen confirms Monday's read rather than changing it. A tape that closes well off its lows, diverges from a green Dow and then resumes flat on the futures reopen is behaving as a sector rotation, not an index breakdown. Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON with a green status for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The flagged danger window spans 13:30Z-14:30Z on 25 August, covering the US cash open and the 14:00Z Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster; every forecast hour still maps to EA_ON because those releases are medium-impact and the conditional Tail peak of 18 stays inside the low band. The named conditional risks for the overnight window are an Asian second leg in memory names at the Tokyo and Seoul opens and the active US-Iran confrontation around the Strait of Hormuz.
headline: CME futures reopen flat near the pre-halt print after a memory-led Nasdaq-100 de-rating, holding Tail at 8 while a Tier-1-free Tuesday calendar lets Stress ease back into the moderate band
body: The defining evidence for this hour is the reopen itself. CME equity futures resumed trading at 22:00Z and the first prints sit around 29,135, within a handful of points of the 29,131.25 pre-halt level, on only a few hundred contracts. There is no reopen gap and no directional extension, which is the structural opposite of the persistent no-retracement path the Tail measure is built to detect. Monday's cash session ended the same way: the Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,023.18, down 285.68 points or 0.98%, inside a 28,875.97-29,151.97 range and roughly 147 points above the session low, while the Dow finished up 0.26% and the S&P 500 lost only 0.28%. That divergence identifies the day as a memory-led semiconductor de-rating rather than a broad index breakdown: the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell more than 3%, Micron lost 5.83%, Nvidia 2.91% and Broadcom 2.63%, yet Meta, Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Apple all closed higher. Cross-asset confirmation for a genuine risk event is absent. VIX rose 4.76% to 15.85 but stayed inside a narrow 15.61-16.06 band and remains in a low-teens regime. The 10-year yield eased about 3.5 basis points to roughly 4.70% against a 4.24% two-year, and WTI fell 2.35% to about 85.02 with Brent at 92.06, declining even as the Treasury rolled out its broadest Iran sanctions package to date. The delayed cross-asset context collected at 22:10Z showed NQ, ES and YM futures within 0.13% of unchanged and Treasury futures near flat, consistent with an orderly handover rather than an overnight repricing. Tail is scored 8 in the low band because none of the amplifiers that define a lethal path are present: no gap, no session-extreme holding, no repeated extension after failed retracements, and no aligned yield, volatility or energy confirmation. Stress eases to 43 in the moderate band because the forward horizon is unusually clean. Tuesday's US calendar is medium-impact only, with Fed Barkin at 12:00Z, Case-Shiller at 13:00Z and a Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster at 14:00Z; the Tier-1 stack of Core PCE, GDP, Durable Goods and Nvidia's results all falls on Wednesday, beyond this horizon. Two conditional risks remain named rather than scored: an Asian second leg in memory names at the Tokyo and Seoul opens, and the active US-Iran confrontation around the Strait of Hormuz, which is the credible discontinuity channel during thin overnight liquidity even though Monday's oil tape showed no transmission. Confidence is 85, supported by verified index, futures, volatility, yield, energy and calendar levels, and limited only by the delayed nature of the post-halt futures feed and the single reopen print available so far.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The window opened at 22:00Z on 23 August with Tail 15 and Stress 45 as Asian technology first repriced the memory-cost story, then settled into a 7-12 band overnight with Stress reaching a window low of 38. The structural peak came in European and early US hours: Tail reached 19 with Stress 58 in a trend-down mode at 07:00Z, eased to 11-13 in a mixed mode through the European morning, stepped to 20 at 13:00Z ahead of the cash open and reached the window's only non-green slot at 14:00Z with Tail 26, Stress 60 and a trend-down mode mapping to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. That reading reversed within one hour: 15:00Z printed Tail 13 as the opening decline retraced, and the series then decayed steadily through the US afternoon to 7-9 with Stress holding at 45. Twenty-three of the 24 slots mapped to EA_ON, one to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES, and the mode migrated from normal through trend-down to mixed.
outlookSummary: The conditional path stays inside the low Tail band for all 24 hours, so every slot maps to EA_ON. It opens at 8 for the observed futures reopen, lifts to 11 at 00:00Z when the Tokyo and Seoul cash opens reprice memory costs most directly, then eases through the Asian session to the horizon floor of 7 at 05:00Z in the inter-session gap before the European pre-open, which also carries the lowest conditional Stress of 40. The European open and morning lift the series to an overnight peak of 12 at 08:00Z, after which it consolidates in a 9-11 band into the US premarket. The horizon peak of 18 falls at 14:00Z, the only event/whipsaw slot, covering the US cash open and the 14:00Z Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster; conditional Stress peaks there at 55. The series then decays through the US afternoon to 10-12, lifts modestly to 12 for the 20:00Z power hour with Barkin speaking again and hedging ahead of Wednesday's releases, and returns to 8 at 21:00Z for the cash close and the CME maintenance halt. No Tier-1 US release falls inside the horizon; Core PCE, GDP, Durable Goods and Nvidia's results all land on Wednesday, beyond it.
